questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go on exchange to an university with a remarkable science faculty with courses that suited my education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, I was contacted by McMaster in advance upon my arrival with the necessary information and I got connected to a contact person to whom I could ask any question.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, the university had a welcome week which was not suited for exchange students but more first-year students. There were also an international day were you met other exchange students from other contries which was beneficial.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my accommodation a good time in advance upon my arrival. I rented an airbnb with to other danish girls in Downtown Hamilton - 15 minutes bus ride from campus. This was perfect.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Hamilton downtown is a harsh environment to live in, a lot of homeless people and drugs on the streets - just be prepared because it is way different than Denmark, but I never felt unsafe.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I know some of my fellow danish exchange students had a hard time to get campus accommodation, so be prepared to look for off-campus accommodation, and watch out for scammers on Facebook groups.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to fill in an application for McMaster after receiving your confirmation from UCPH, this was straight forward. When registering for courses you were provided with a detailed guide how to do so, and you were provided with a feature where you could select different courses and see their time schedule and watch if they overlapped.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was connected with a person from the Health Science faculty, where I beforehand sent her a list of 8 courses I maybe wanted to take, and she told me which I could take or not.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was really succesfull I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to checkout which courses are offered in which semester, and have an idea which courses you want to take - you will spare a lot of time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 third-year courses and 1 fourth-year course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to do a lot of quizzes, assignments, presentations and so on. Compared to my study - molecular biomedicine - where only the final exam count, everything counted in you final grade - every quiz, midterms, presentations and so on.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
3MI3 - Microbial Interaction
3K03 = Principle of Virology
3I03 = Introduction to Immunology
4E03 = Gene regulation in stem cell and development.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
3I03 = the teachers and assistants were amazing - such a pleasure to be reached by them. Made a complex topic easy to understand. and no exam :))
3K03= Dr. Mullarkey was amazing, it was interesting and fun to learn about different viruses - based on principles and not memorizing details.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay for health insurance at the university.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Local transportation, almost every bus in Hamilton is free for students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you could imagine - it is easy to sign up and find.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The outdoor club - amazing hikes and canoe trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to toronto, Algonquin park, Bruce peninsula, New York. For Christmas there is also a lot of Christmas markets.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, just have to get used to the currency.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Be open, participates in events at campus, connect with your classmates and other exchange students.
Canadians are really nice and openminded - so be likewise

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I was not prepared for the harsh environment that exist in Canada, there are a lot of homeless people and drug addicts. They don't do anything but on this point just be prepared.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly the locals were.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring an adapter, be openminded and don't freak out over the size of the campus - you will eventually learn where to go.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Coffee is cheap, Mills library is good to study at, food at campus is expensive - so bring your own lunch :))

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I have met. I have learned so much about other contries and cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not missing home and the time differences. In my case the home-sicking disappeared after a month - until I got into a new routine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
